about:
What the system ssh wrote to stderr, and its exit code, for each way a connection to a host fails (#120, L1). “recorded” entries ran OpenSSH_10.3p1 (LibreSSL 3.3.6, macOS) with -F /dev/null -o BatchMode=yes -o ControlPath=none -T and no usable key, against a public SSH server, a closed local port, an unroutable address and a name that doesn’t resolve; the host names, user names, addresses, file paths and the key fingerprint were replaced. ssh ends each line with 
 when it writes to a pipe. “probe” entries come from the remote-hosts probe runs on a Linux host (P6, a frozen host with ServerAliveInterval=15), host name removed. “documented” entries are built from the format strings in openssh-portable’s source (cited), since they weren’t recorded.

failures.name: resolve
failures.stderr: ssh: Could not resolve hostname host.example.com: nodename nor servname provided, or not known

failures.name: resolve-linux
failures.source: documented: sshconnect.c, “%s: Could not resolve hostname %.100s: %s” with glibc’s gai_strerror(EAI_NONAME)
failures.stderr: ssh: Could not resolve hostname host.example.com: Name or service not known

failures.name: refused
failures.stderr: ssh: connect to host host.example.com port 22: Connection refused

failures.name: timed-out
failures.stderr: ssh: connect to host host.example.com port 22: Operation timed out

failures.name: timed-out-linux
failures.source: documented: sshconnect.c, “ssh: connect to host %s port %s: %s” with Linux’s strerror(ETIMEDOUT)
failures.stderr: ssh: connect to host host.example.com port 22: Connection timed out

failures.name: network-unreachable
failures.source: documented: sshconnect.c, “ssh: connect to host %s port %s: %s” with strerror(ENETUNREACH)
failures.stderr: ssh: connect to host host.example.com port 22: Network is unreachable

failures.name: keepalive-drop
failures.source: probe: P6, ssh exited 255 about 56 s after the host froze, with ServerAliveInterval=15 and ServerAliveCountMax=3; host name removed
failures.stderr:
** WARNING: connection is not using a post-quantum key exchange algorithm.
** This session may be vulnerable to "store now, decrypt later" attacks.
** The server may need to be upgraded. See https://openssh.com/pq.html
Timeout, server host.example.com not responding.

failures.name: closed-by-remote
failures.source: documented: packet.c, “Connection closed by %s”, where %s is “<address> port <port>”

failures.name: sign-in
failures.stderr:
Warning: Permanently added 'host.example.com' (ED25519) to the list of known hosts.
no such identity: /Users/user/.ssh/id_ed25519: No such file or directory
user@host.example.com: Permission denied (publickey).

failures.name: sign-in-methods
failures.source: documented: sshconnect2.c, “%s@%s: Permission denied (%s).” with the server’s list of methods

failures.name: host-key-unknown
failures.source: recorded: StrictHostKeyChecking at its default, ask, which BatchMode can’t ask

failures.name: host-key-unknown-strict
failures.stderr:
No ED25519 host key is known for host.example.com and you have requested strict checking.
Host key verification failed.

failures.name: host-key-changed
failures.source: recorded: a known_hosts line with another key for the host
failures.stderr:
@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
@    WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!     @
@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
IT IS POSSIBLE THAT SOMEONE IS DOING SOMETHING NASTY!
Someone could be eavesdropping on you right now (man-in-the-middle attack)!
It is also possible that a host key has just been changed.
The fingerprint for the ED25519 key sent by the remote host is
SHA256:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA.
Please contact your system administrator.
Add correct host key in /Users/user/.ssh/known_hosts to get rid of this message.
Offending ED25519 key in /Users/user/.ssh/known_hosts:3
Host key for host.example.com has changed and you have requested strict checking.
Host key verification failed.

failures.name: not-installed
failures.source: recorded: bash 3.2 on macOS running the fixed command with -c, as sshd runs it through the login shell; home folder replaced
failures.stderr: bash: /home/user/.postbox-remote/0.10.0/server/remote/host/host: No such file or directory

failures.name: not-installed-bash5
failures.source: documented: bash 5 adds “line N:” for -c, as the probe’s “p1.sh: line 30: klist: command not found” shows
failures.stderr: bash: line 1: /home/user/.postbox-remote/0.10.0/server/remote/host/host: No such file or directory

failures.name: other
failures.source: documented: readconf.c, “%s: line %d: Bad configuration option: %s” and “%s: terminating, %d bad configuration options”, from a ~/.ssh/config ssh can’t read
failures.stderr:
/Users/user/.ssh/config: line 4: Bad configuration option: frobnicate
/Users/user/.ssh/config: terminating, 1 bad configuration options
